description: Enhanced HANA semantics for Finance (FI/CO) AI agent use cases. Covers G/L, AR/AP, Fixed Assets, CO-OM, Treasury, MM/SD integration, and master data. Includes semantic definitions for key financial metrics such as revenue, expenses, assets, and liabilities. Revenue accounts: 800000 (Domestic), 805000 (Export).

BKPF.description: Accounting document header (FI). Stores one row per financial posting document with metadata such as company code, fiscal year, posting date, and currency. CRITICAL FOR AGING REPORTS: BUDAT (posting date) is in this table, NOT in BSEG. For AR/AP aging queries, you MUST join BSEG with BKPF on MANDT, BUKRS, BELNR, GJAHR to access BUDAT for age calculations. Never reference BUDAT directly from BSEG.

BELNR.meaning: Unique identifier of the financial document within company code and fiscal year.

BUKRS.meaning: Organizational unit representing an independent legal entity for external reporting.

GJAHR.meaning: The financial year to which the document belongs.

BLART.meaning: Categorizes the business transaction (e.g., invoice, payment, adjustment).

BUDAT.meaning: The date on which the transaction is recorded in the general ledger.

BLDAT.meaning: The date of the original source document (e.g., invoice date).

POPER.meaning: The fiscal period (1–12 or 1–16) to which the posting is assigned.

WAERS.meaning: ISO currency code of the transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, CNY).

KURSF.meaning: Rate used to convert document currency to local currency at posting time.

XBLNR.meaning: External reference such as vendor invoice number or check number.

STBLG.meaning: If populated, indicates this document has been reversed by the referenced document.

STJAH.meaning: Fiscal year of the reversal document.

XREVERSAL.meaning: Flags whether this document is a reversal or has been reversed.

AWTYP.meaning: The originating SAP transaction or module that created this document.

AWKEY.meaning: Concatenated key linking back to the source transaction (e.g., MM invoice + year).

USNAM.meaning: SAP user ID of the person who posted the document.

TCODE.meaning: The T-code used to create the document.

BSEG.description: Accounting document segment (FI). Line-item details for each financial posting, split by company code, fiscal year, and document number. IMPORTANT: BUDAT (posting date) is NOT in this table. For date calculations and aging reports, you MUST join with DBADMIN.BKPF on MANDT, BUKRS, BELNR, GJAHR to access BUDAT from the header table. For Accounts Receivable aging, join with BKPF to access BUDAT, use KUNNR for customer, filter KOART='D' and open items via NULL/empty AUGBL. For Accounts Payable aging, use LIFNR instead of KUNNR. Revenue line items are identified by KOART='S' and SHKZG='H'. Open items are identified by NULL or empty AUGBL.

BUZEI.meaning: Sequential line number within the document (typically 1, 2, 3…).

HKONT.meaning: The G/L account number being debited or credited.
HKONT.business_note: Revenue accounts are typically 800000 (Domestic) and 805000 (Export). Join with SKA1/SKAT to classify by account type.

DMBTR.meaning: Monetary value in the company code's local currency.
DMBTR.business_note: For AR aging (KOART='D', KUNNR populated): DMBTR is positive for both invoices (SHKZG='S') and payments (SHKZG='H'). Use CASE WHEN SHKZG='S' THEN DMBTR ELSE -DMBTR END to get the signed amount affecting the customer balance. For revenue lines (KOART='S', SHKZG='H'), this represents the revenue amount. Note: DMBTR is positive for debits and negative for credits in some configurations; verify sign convention when aggregating revenue.

WRBTR.meaning: Monetary value in the transaction's original currency.

SHKZG.meaning: Determines whether the line is a debit or credit.
SHKZG.business_note: For Accounts Receivable (KUNNR populated, KOART='D'): SHKZG='S' represents invoices (increases receivable), SHKZG='H' represents payments/credit memos (decreases receivable). Net amount = CASE WHEN SHKZG='S' THEN DMBTR ELSE -DMBTR END. For Accounts Payable (LIFNR populated, KOART='K'): SHKZG='H' represents invoices (increases payable), SHKZG='S' represents payments (decreases payable).

KOART.meaning: The type of account being posted to.
KOART.business_note: For AR queries, use KOART='D' with KUNNR populated. For AP queries, use KOART='K' with LIFNR populated. For revenue queries, use KOART='S' with HKONT in revenue account ranges.

LIFNR.meaning: Linked vendor (creditor) master record for payables postings.

KUNNR.meaning: Linked customer (debtor) master record for receivables postings.

KOSTL.meaning: Cost center charged with the expense or revenue.

AUFNR.meaning: Internal order charged with the expense or revenue.

PRCTR.meaning: Profit center responsible for the line item's financial result.

GSBER.meaning: Cross-company-code organizational unit for segment reporting.

SGTXT.meaning: Free-text description or memo for the line item.

ZUONR.meaning: Key used for automatic clearing and matching of open items.

MWSKZ.meaning: Determines tax treatment (input/output, rate, exempt) for the line item.

VALUT.meaning: The date used for bank interest calculation and cash-flow planning.

PROJK.meaning: Work breakdown structure element for project accounting.

AUGBL.meaning: Document number that cleared this open item.
AUGBL.business_note: For open items reports (AR/AP aging), filter where AUGBL IS NULL or TRIM(AUGBL) = '' to get only unpaid items. When AUGBL is populated, the line item has been cleared/paid.

AUGDT.meaning: Date on which the open item was cleared.

CSKS.description: Cost center master data (CO-OM-CCA). Defines cost centers within a controlling area for overhead allocation and internal reporting.

KOKRS.meaning: The highest organizational unit in Management Accounting (CO).

KOSTL.meaning: Unique identifier for a department or function that incurs costs.

DATBI.meaning: End of the validity period for this master record (usually 9999-12-31 if active).

KOSAR.meaning: Grouping of cost centers by function (e.g., production, administration, sales).

VERAK.meaning: Name or user ID of the cost center manager.

WAERS.meaning: Currency used for cost center planning and reporting.

PRCTR.meaning: Profit center to which the cost center belongs for profitability reporting.

CSKT.description: Cost center descriptions (language-dependent text). Multilingual names and descriptions for cost centers.

SPRAS.meaning: Language code per ISO 639-1 (e.g., EN for English, DE for German).
SPRAS.business_note: Must be a two-letter ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., EN, DE). Single-letter codes like 'E' are not valid.

KTEXT.meaning: Short descriptive name of the cost center.

LTEXT.meaning: Extended description or notes for the cost center.

FAGLFLEXA.description: General ledger line items (New G/L, FAGL). Document-segment view for financial reporting. Contains detailed revenue and expense line items. Revenue line items have RACCT in ('800000','805000') and DRCRK='H'. Amount field HSL is the local currency amount (company code currency). TSL is transaction currency. HSL is stored as negative for credit entries (including revenue), so use -HSL to get positive revenue amounts.

RLDNR.meaning: Ledger identifier (e.g., 0L = leading ledger, NL = non-leading ledger).

BELNR.meaning: The accounting document number in the leading ledger.

DOCLN.meaning: Line item number within the document.

RACCT.meaning: General ledger account number posted in this line.
RACCT.business_note: Revenue accounts are typically 800000 (Domestic) and 805000 (Export). Expense accounts are typically in the range 420000-480000. Use RACCT IN ('800000','805000') to filter revenue line items and RACCT BETWEEN '420000' AND '480000' to filter expense line items. To get account descriptions (e.g., for expense categorization), join with SKAT on RACCT = SAKNR to access the TXT50 field. Note: While SKA1 contains the master data for G/L accounts, SKAT contains the language-dependent descriptions (TXT50) needed for text-based categorization. When filtering SKAT by language, use SPRAS = 'EN' (two-letter ISO code), not 'E'.

KOSTL.meaning: Cost center dimension for overhead allocation and internal reporting.

DRCRK.business_note: Revenue line items in FAGLFLEXA have DRCRK='H' (Credit). Use DRCRK='H' with RACCT IN ('800000','805000') to identify revenue lines.

HSL.business_note: Stored as negative for credit entries (including revenue). Use -HSL to get positive revenue amounts.

TSL.meaning: Amount in the original transaction currency.
TSL.business_note: Stored as negative for credit entries (including revenue). Use -TSL to get positive revenue amounts.

RTCUR.meaning: Currency key of the original transaction.

POPER.meaning: The fiscal period (1–12 or 1–16) to which the posting is assigned.

BUDAT.meaning: The date on which the transaction is recorded in the general ledger.

BLART.meaning: Categorizes the business transaction (e.g., invoice, payment, adjustment).

FAGLFLEXT.description: General ledger totals (New G/L, FAGL). Aggregated balances per G/L account, company code, fiscal year, and additional dimensions such as profit center and segment. Contains summarized balance totals (e.g., trial balance figures). For detailed transaction-level financial statements (e.g., line-item balance sheets or P&L statements), query FAGLFLEXA instead. Revenue line totals can be identified by RACCT in ('800000','805000') and RLDNR='0L' (leading ledger). Note: TSLVT is opening balance in transaction currency; TSL01-TSL16 are period totals. For revenue trends, use TSL01-TSL16 (period totals) rather than carry-forward fields.

KNA1.description: Customer master data (general data, FI-AR / SD). General information about customers including name, address, and tax data.

KUNNR.meaning: Unique identifier for the customer across the client.

NAME1.meaning: Unique identifier for the customer across the client.

STCD1.meaning: Primary tax identification number (e.g., VAT ID, EIN).

KTOKD.meaning: Grouping controlling field status and number range (e.g., domestic, foreign, one-time).

LFA1.description: Vendor master data (general data, FI-AP / MM). General information about vendors including name, address, and tax data.

LIFNR.meaning: Unique identifier for the vendor across the client.

NAME1.meaning: Primary name of the vendor or supplier.

STCD1.meaning: Primary tax identification number (e.g., VAT ID, EIN).

KTOKK.meaning: Grouping that controls master data fields and number range (e.g., domestic, foreign, one-time).

SPERM.meaning: If set, no postings are allowed to this vendor.

SETHEADERT.description: Hierarchy header descriptions (language-dependent text). Text for hierarchy nodes and sets used in reporting hierarchies.

SPRAS.meaning: Language code per ISO 639-1 (e.g., EN for English, DE for German).
SPRAS.business_note: Must be a two-letter ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., EN, DE). Single-letter codes like 'E' are not valid.

TEXT.meaning: Human-readable name of the hierarchy node.

SETLEAF.description: Hierarchy set leaves (CO-OM). Stores leaf-node values in account assignment hierarchies such as cost-center groups or G/L account groups.

SETLEAF.meaning: The actual account, cost center, or other object at this leaf.

SEQNR.meaning: Order of the leaf within the hierarchy node.

SUBSET.meaning: If the leaf is itself a subset (nested hierarchy), this references the sub-set ID.

SETNODE.description: Hierarchy set nodes (CO-OM). Stores node values in account assignment hierarchies such as cost-center groups or G/L account groups.

NODEID.meaning: Identifier of the node within the hierarchy.

SETLEAF.meaning: Indicates whether the node is a leaf node in the hierarchy.

SEQNR.meaning: Order of the node within the hierarchy node.

SKA1.description: G/L account master data (chart of accounts level). Defines every general ledger account in the chart of accounts.

SAKNR.meaning: Unique account number within the chart of accounts.
SAKNR.business_note: Values 800000-805000 typically represent revenue accounts (800000 = domestic revenue, 805000 = export revenue). Use SAKNR IN ('800000','805000') to identify revenue accounts in BSEG or FAGLFLEXA.

TXT50.meaning: Short text describing the account's purpose (e.g., 'Cash in Bank').
TXT50.business_note: Revenue accounts typically have descriptions containing words like 'Revenue', 'Sales', 'Export', or 'Domestic Sales'. Use TXT50 with KTOPL to identify revenue accounts when SAKNR is not sufficient.

XBILK.meaning: Whether the account appears on the balance sheet (asset/liability/equity) or P&L.

GVTYP.meaning: Grouping that controls field status and number range (e.g., assets, liabilities, expenses).

XOPVW.meaning: If set, the account tracks individual open items for clearing.

MUZAH.meaning: Whether line items can be displayed directly from the account.

SKAT.description: G/L account descriptions (language-dependent text). Provides multilingual descriptions for chart-of-accounts accounts.

SPRAS.meaning: Language code per ISO 639-1 (e.g., EN for English, DE for German).
SPRAS.business_note: Must be a two-letter ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., EN, DE). Single-letter codes like 'E' are not valid.

T001.description: Company codes (FI organizational master). Defines independent legal entities for external financial reporting.

BUTXT.meaning: Full legal or operating name of the company.

LAND1.meaning: ISO country code (e.g., US, DE, CN) determining legal and tax rules.

WAERS.meaning: Local currency (company code currency) for all postings.

SPRAS.meaning: Language code per ISO 639-1 (e.g., EN for English, DE for German).
SPRAS.business_note: Must be a two-letter ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., EN, DE). Single-letter codes like 'E' are not valid.

PERIV.meaning: Defines the number of posting periods and special periods (e.g., K4 = calendar year, V3 = Apr–Mar).

KTOPL.meaning: The chart of accounts assigned to this company code.

XMWST.meaning: Whether the company is registered for VAT/sales tax.

T001W.description: Plants / Locations (MM-SD-PP organizational master). Assignment of plants to company codes for inventory and production.

WERKS.meaning: Unique identifier for a production facility, warehouse, or distribution center.

BUKRS.meaning: Company code to which the plant belongs financially.

FABKL.meaning: Calendar defining working days, holidays, and shift schedules for the plant.

REGIO.meaning: State or province code within the country.

ORT01.meaning: City where the plant is located.

TCURC.description: Currency pairs (FI). Defines which currency pairs are valid for exchange rate maintenance.

CURRKEY_TO.meaning: ISO currency code for the target currency.

TCURR.description: Exchange rates (FI). Stores currency conversion rates between source and target currencies for specific validity dates.

GDATU.meaning: Date from which this exchange rate is effective.

KURST.meaning: Category of rate (e.g., M = middle rate, B = buying rate, G = selling rate, EURX = euro translation).
